data.narrative:
Quindar, a Series A space & aerospace company founded by Matthew Regan, Zach Meza, David Lawrence, Sandilya Bhagavathula, Shaishav Parekh, and Nate Hamet, has raised $27.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 5 public tickers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage peers in the same sector.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding $55M. Peer-median triangulation across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B Series B), Aalyria ($1.3B Series B), and Starcloud ($1.1B Seed)—produces a median of $1.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue. The public Space & Aerospace sector trades at a median 24.4x price-to-sales across the five tickers, but lacks applicability without target financials.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $46M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $677M. The extreme width reflects structural uncertainty: stage-progression yields a conservative floor based on capital deployed, while peer-median reflects substantial upside embedded in comparable valuations at adjacent stages. Key uncertainties include Quindar's revenue trajectory, customer traction, and technical differentiation relative to the peer set. Resolution of these factors would narrow the range considerably.
